title: Register-aware phrasing: bare noun-compound density vs pithy/accessible dial

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Prompted by a real catch: 'thrift family' shipped in an Anth.us post where
'family of thrift' would have read more natural/accessible. Ryan asked
whether the underlying pattern is deterministically detectable and whether
register preference (pithy/insider vs accessible/explainer) could be a
per-profile toggle that shapes what the scanner surfaces, rather than left
to agent judgment each time.

THE PATTERN: bare noun-compound premodification ("thrift family," "cost
basis," "risk profile") vs. of-genitive postmodification ("family of
thrift"). English uses both constantly and correctly -- "data center,"
"style guide," "product manager" are fine bare compounds nobody wants
flagged. Dense STACKS of bare compounding read as jargony/insider; the
"of" form spells out the relationship, reading slower but more accessible.

WHY THIS ISN'T A SIMPLE REGEX: unlike bannedPhrases/bannedIntensifiers
(exact strings), telling "fine compound" from "insider-dense compound"
apart in general requires actually knowing which words are nouns and how
they're chunking -- i.e. real POS tagging / noun-phrase chunking. Limatus
has deliberately stayed dependency-light (PyYAML only); this would be the
first real NLP dependency.

TWO PATHS, not one:

1. Near-term, zero new dependencies: generalize the mechanism already used
   for this exact fix into a reusable profile field -- `preferredPhrasing:
   [{from, to}]` per style-profile.yml, mechanically identical to
   bannedPatterns but framed as reword-not-ban. Catches known repeat
   offenders (a publication's own list of insider shorthand it wants
   unpacked), zero false-positive risk, but doesn't generalize to novel
   compounds it hasn't seen before.

2. Real capability, real epic: a compound-noun density heuristic (POS
   tagging + noun-phrase chunking), scored per paragraph/document, with a
   profile-level register dial (e.g. `checks.compoundNounDensity: pithy |
   neutral | accessible` or a numeric threshold) that changes what fires as
   a finding. Bigger lift: new dependency choice (spaCy is heavy; something
   lighter -- a small rule-based POS tagger -- might be enough for
   English-only noun-compound detection), needs a real fixture corpus of
   "insider-dense" vs "accessible" paragraphs to tune against, and needs to
   not fight existing checks (uniformCadence, vagueClaim) that already
   touch related territory.

RECOMMENDATION: do (1) now, cheaply, next time a specific compound repeats
across a publication's drafts (same pattern as how bannedPhrases/lexicon
entries get added -- reactively, from real catches). Scope (2) as its own
epic under this one, gated on someone actually wanting the general
register-dial capability badly enough to justify the new dependency --
don't build the POS-tagging machinery speculatively.

Filed as LIM-74d5fb under the quality-first editorial rewrite loop epic
(LIM-9d14e6) rather than as its own top-level epic, since it's squarely a
new *kind* of check within that existing scope, not a new capability area.
